html:
SMTO-CFG-0074 — The thinking target must be a whole number from 0 to 100

GUID: 6aa83a98-4da7-4aa3-b984-2d0fce700c84
Slug: thinking-budget-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The share of each response the Agent may spend thinking is set to something other than a whole number from 0 to 100, so SMTO stopped before starting the task or schedule.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and set Thinking target (%) to a whole number between 0 and 100, such as 50. This saved default is used by every new task, and a value outside that range stops tasks from starting.
  2. In the conversation, if you see a Default button next to the thinking slider in the message box, select it. This clears any value set just for this conversation, so the setting from step 1 is used.
  3. If a script, another program or a schedule starts tasks for you, ask the person who set it up to send the thinking target as a whole number from 0 to 100. Those requests can carry their own value, which SMTO checks the same way.
  4. Open the conversation to check that the task didn't start, then send it again. Checking first makes sure you don't run the same work twice.

What success looks like

  • The task starts and the thinking slider in the message box shows a percentage from 0 to 100.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change other limits, such as Maximum completion tokens or timeouts; they aren't the cause. An older task keeps the value it started with, so start it as a new task instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • llm_reasoning_budget_percent is not an exact integer from 0 through 100 (from runtime controls, conversation values, a schedule or a resumed run's saved state).

What this means

  • The reasoning-budget percentage is not an exact integer between zero and 100 inclusive. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • The reasoning-budget percentage is not an exact integer between zero and 100 inclusive.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the value's exact type and percent units rather than supplying a token count.

How to fix it

  • Correct llm_reasoning_budget_percent to an integer 0–100 (booleans and decimals are rejected) in the runtime controls (Settings › Setup › Model routing › Thinking target (%)), the conversation's composer profile, the schedule or API request, or AOR_LLM_REASONING_BUDGET_PERCENT. Accepted and resumed runs keep the value they captured, so only new tasks pick up the change.
  • Set Thinking budget (%) within that range and check whether the task captures this preference at creation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported percentage is accepted in its owning task/control scope.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
